content.thinking:
I need to examine the brandId function for use when listing org IDs.

The overdue job workspace listing currently relies on `usageRepo.listOrgIdsForRollup`, which misses brand new organizations that lack usage rows. I will add a `listLiveOrgIds` method to the organization repository that filters out archived organizations. I am also considering whether this function should accept a `shouldFilterArchived` parameter.

The overdue job already validates archive scope with `shouldFilterArchived(LIVE_ONLY)`. I will use the base repository's `livePredicate` for the new `listLiveOrgIds` method.

The 50-org batch limit risks skipping brand-new workspaces and older organizations. The job must cover every workspace without a hard cap, so pagination is required.

I will fetch all non-deleted organizations without a batch limit. Existing tests remain valid.

I am designing the overdue issue tracking logic. The `reported` set must only announce issues that are newly overdue compared to the previous sweep.

I am implementing the `overdueLastSweep` tracking set and a `resetOverdueTracking` helper. The job function fetches live organization IDs and initializes a `new Set<string>()` to collect overdue issues for the current sweep.

The job iterates over each live organization and queries overdue issues. It skips items with null due dates, archived status, closed status, or a due date at or after the sweep timestamp. It adds newly overdue issues to the current sweep set and only emits notifications for issues absent from the previous sweep.

I realized the tracking logic has a subtle bug.

The tracking logic handles success, failure, and job crashes correctly. A critical bug remains: replacing the entire `overdueLastSweep` set at the end of the job is unsafe if `listLiveOrgIds` fails partway through.

The reported set is shared across tests, so updating it only at the end of a full sweep preserves correct behavior. The user's described bug occurs because the set never drops IDs, meaning an issue that was announced and then canceled or reopened will never be re-announced.

Listing all live organizations prevents skipping workspaces that contain overdue issues. The replacement set also resolves the edge case where an issue remains overdue across multiple sweeps.

If an organization is deleted, its overdue issues are naturally excluded from the current sweep. They will be re-announced if the organization is restored later.

Failed emissions will remain out of the tracking set so the next sweep retries them.

I am weighing whether to keep failed emissions out of the tracking set. If an emission fails, the issue was found overdue but not announced, so the next sweep should announce it. However, the user's rule says later sweeps must not re-announce an issue unless every sweep in between also found it overdue.

I will keep failed emissions out of the tracking set. A strict reading of the rule would lock alerts forever if the first announcement fails, so retries are safer. The streak should count only successful finds.

I will add an issue to the current sweep set only after a successful announcement, or if it was already present in the previous sweep. This preserves the streak for issues that were previously tracked while allowing failed emissions to be retried.
Checking whether Drizzle supports a notInArray operator.
I am examining the inbox filter more carefully.
Checking whether notifications are being filed under the wrong workspace. The notify function uses the event's organization, but the preference or insert might use a different one.

Two alert preference bugs were found. Users who disabled overdue alerts still receive due soon alerts, and vice versa, because the code checks the wrong preference key. I also need to verify that getPreference filters by organization correctly, since alerts should remain within their own workspace.

The organization filtering checks out. The notification service uses orgPredicate and payload.orgId, so alerts stay scoped to the correct workspace. The overdue handler correctly skips assertOrgScope because no actor is present.

The inbox filter is not the culprit. The only filing location is notification-service.ts line 195, which is the bug.

I also need to watch the sweep re-announce test. resetOverdueTracking only runs in beforeAll, so the reported set accumulates across tests and could break the "emits issue.overdue once" assertion.

The reported set persists across test files because resetOverdueTracking only runs in beforeAll. jobs.test.ts also calls runOverdueIssueJob without resetting state, so its "emits once" assertion may fail if both files run in the same vitest worker.

The reported set persists across test files, so jobs.test.ts still counts only newly processed issues. If test files are isolated, each starts with an empty set and the same single-issue result holds.

The test that runs the job twice and expects one emission is handled correctly. The first test in the file creates a single overdue issue, so if the reported set is empty it will be counted as new. Because beforeAll only resets state once, any prior issues from earlier tests in the same file would already be in the set and skipped.

The remaining sweep tests check out. Closed and no-due-date issues are skipped correctly. The "emits once" assertion passes because prior issues are already in the reported set. Re-emit and multi-org tests also behave as expected.

Listing all live organizations each sweep ensures every overdue issue is evaluated. Previously skipped organizations without usage rows will now be included.
Checking STATUS_CYCLE to see if canceled issues can be overdue in seed.
Checking whether drizzle-orm exports a notInArray helper.
The `notInArray` method might not be available in this version of Drizzle.
